newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - Looking to India.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - Looking to India.

text.p: Gulf oil product markets are unlikely to be shaken from current ranges before Indian Oil Corp (IOC) issues its next major gas oil (diesel) buying tender for April delivery, Gulf traders said on Thursday.
"It's the new fiscal year in India and budgets for oil imports could be relaxed," said one trader, anticipating that the state oil firm would be in a better fiscal position to increase imports.
IOC last month bought 615,000 tonnes of high speed diesel in its March tender compared to 915-960,000 tonnes in March 1996.

The state firm took 750-800,000 tonnes of diesel in April last year, well above the 450,000 tonnes in April 1995 and traders expect no slow-down in Indian distillate demand even after the recent partial removal of subsidies on local prices.
"Cargoes are already being pinpointed in the hope that IOC will buck this market...we could see them restocking," another trader said.
April's tender is to be awarded at the end of February.
IOC was also expected in the coming days to award two cargoes totalling 80-90,000 tonnes of 0.5 percent sulphur for March delivery. Nepal was also in the market for distillates.
Gas oil held steady at $23.00-$23.50 a barrel fob Gulf range this month. Premiums to quotes are unchanged at 50-60 cents.
The gas oil-jet spread has widened out to 13-month highs as firm Asian jet markets pushed Gulf jet-kerosene out to $29.10 a barrel from $28.80 the previous week.

Gulf naphtha has been the strongest performer and is not expected to lose ground because of strong Far East feedstock demand, traders said. Naphtha for March delivery reached $211.50 a tonne fob Gulf on Thursday, a 2.5 percent gain on the week.
Naphtha's premium to price quotes was at $13-14 on strong Asian import demand, traders said.
Trading in the region is expected to pick up after the Moslem holy fasting month of Ramadan which is expected to end this weekend.
